newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends mixed in dull trade, nearbys gain.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends mixed in dull trade, nearbys gain.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mixed in quiet trading on Thursday, with the nearby contracts managing to post modest gains on the heels of the market's recent downturn.

September arabicas rose 1.45 cents per lb on the day, to 184.55 cents, after ranging from 186.75 to 180.00 cents. Active December gained 0.55 cent, to 166.05 cents, while the back months closed down 0.10 to 0.60 cent.

Dealers said trade buying of the nearby switches helped to steady the market. September/December widened to 18.50 cents compared with 17.60 cents at the close on Tuesday. December/March 1998 stretched to 16.85 cents versus 16.20 cents the previous session.
"The market recovered on interest in the switches more than anything else," said one trader. "But nothing much really happened today."

Volume on the day was light, at an estimated 4,524 lots, and open interest continued to inch lower. As of August 13, total open interest stood at 20,536 lots, down 343 lots from the previous session. Open interest in September, which enters delivery period in a week, fell by 786 lots, 6,196 lots.
Technically, traders pegged September resistance at 187.00 cents, followed by 188.50 cents and 191.50 cents. On the downside, support was seen at 180.00 cents, then 177.50 cents and 175.00 cents.
Traders await the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock report due after the close on Friday.

Most industry sources expect the data to show a fairly modest build in U.S. green coffee inventories during July. Industry estimates have called for an increase of 50,000 to 150,000 60-kg bags, although some dealers predicted a stock build of up to 250,000 bags.

"They are going to be up and I think a 100,000 increase is fully priced in the market," said a trader. "The significant thing about the GCA stocks and the certified stocks recently is not how much is there but that the trend has been that as the market rallies they have gone back up."

After Thursday's close, the CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 839 60-kg bags as of August 13, to 92,120 bags. There were an additional 5,800 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
